title: Seller fast-lab: compact battle playbook (draft)
content:
TL;DR
A 10–15 minute seller-facing playbook for field engineers and SEs to run a fast pilot and close proof-of-value. Compact, scenario-driven, designed to be memorized and executed on a call or in a 1-hour technical session. Work-in-progress; needs SE feedback and a short internal rehearsal run.

Objective
- Get from discovery -> working pilot in one session (or same-day follow-up).
- Demonstrate: predictable latency, fallback behavior, and a conservative cost anchor.
- Leave with a clear next step: reserved capacity trial or 30-day Pilot SLA.

Primary personas (who uses this)
- Integration Architect (platform/infra lead) — cares about SLAs, routing, VPC/connectivity.
- ML/Inference Engineer — cares about model fidelity, KV cache, batching, quantization.
- Product Manager/PO — cares about business outcome and costs.

Signal checklist (quick qualify)
- Customer has >1000 monthly conversions or latency-sensitive user journeys.
- Wants on-prem/VPC or predictable commit soon.
- Has security/compliance constraints (KMS, audit logs).
If < two signals, default to hosted API trial playbook instead.

One-liner (memorize)
"Redwood gives you predictable, production-grade LLM inference with cost controls and safe fallbacks so your feature stays live even under load."

Elevator technical proof points (two lines)
- Our runtime uses continuous batching + KV caching to reduce per-token cost while keeping 95th latency within SLA.
- We support model variants and automatic fallbacks (quantized model + regional failover) to maintain service during constrained capacity.

Quick demo script (10 minutes)
1) 60s — Problem setup: user flow, SLA target, rough traffic profile.
2) 2m — Show Console: token-level cost, route policy, model pinning UI.
3) 4m — Live call into hosted endpoint demo (short prompt -> streaming response). Show latency numbers and token profiling.
4) 2m — Trigger fallback: simulate capacity error/region fail by toggling route policy in Console; show transparent retry and metrics.
5) 1m — Close: propose next step (pilot + canary checklist).

Pilot offer (mutually agreeable starter)
- 2-week pilot: up to 10M tokens, one dedicated test route, standard support.
- Option to convert to 3-month reserved capacity if throughput > X rps.
- Deliverables: latency report, cost breakdown, canary-run checklist, simple integration guide.

Pricing anchor script
- "For an app with 10k daily users sending ~50 tokens/query, typical hosted usage maps to ~$Y/day; committed dedicated capacity reduces unit cost by ~Z% — we show both numbers in the after-action report."
- Leave a conservative number. Sellers: do not overpromise; use Console numbers.

Objection quick-replies (shortform)
- "We can't take downtime for model updates." -> "We support pinned model versions and canary rollouts with automated fallback to a stable variant — you control the rollout window."
- "We need on-prem because of data" -> "We offer Private deployments with customer-managed control plane and VPC options; we can run a short feasibility scoping call with Infra in <1 week."
- "We already run models in-house" -> "Great. We partner with platform teams: we can run a side-by-side throughput/lambda-cost comparison and show unit-cost delta including operational overhead."

Technical fallback play (how to explain to SREs)
- Primary: route to dedicated pool in same region -> low latency.
- Secondary: route to quantized model variant (smaller memory footprint) -> slightly higher perplexity but stays within SLO.
- Tertiary: regional fallback -> increased latency but preserves uptime.
Note: fallback choices are configurable per-route and visible in console.

Canary & runbook (short)
Pre-canary checklist:
- Integration endpoint reachable (CORS/Firewall rules checked)
- API key with limited scope created and shared with SE
- Baseline prompt set loaded for quality regression checks
Canary run (30–60 mins):
- Run steady ramp to target RPS; monitor 95th latency, error-rate, and token burn.
- Verify KV cache hit rates using Console metrics.
- Execute simulated region failover (optional) and confirm fallback behavior.
Post-canary:
- Collate latency and cost snapshot; add recommendation: batch size, quantization profile.

Playbook for SE during discovery call (script bullets)
- Ask: "What's your 95th percentile latency target for inference?" Note answer.
- Ask: "What volume do you expect (RPS & tokens/query) in peak windows?"
- Ask: "Any regulatory constraints or VPC needs?"
- Offer: "If you want, we can do a 2-week pilot starting with a single route; it usually takes 1 hour to wire in a test route."

Proof materials to drop in follow-up email
- After-action PDF with: latency chart, token-cost breakdown, fallback trace, recommended model profile (quantized vs full).
- Links: quickstart repo, confluence pilot-runbook, SOW template for Dedicated.

Sellers notes to self (raw)
- Keep demo prompts short and representative of customer domain. Avoid showing hallucination edge cases; use controlled eval prompt set.
- If customer asks about model training data: stay policy-correct: we do not train on customer data by default; check Private deployment terms.
- Use "reserved capacity" language only after confirming expected sustained RPS.

Open questions / things to iterate
- Should we bake a standardized 10-prompt eval pack per vertical? (Retail / FinServ / Docs / Chat) -> high priority for Q1 playbook.
- Need a one-page SLA quicksheet for rapid email follow-up.
- Add a 1-click Console macro to simulate fallback during demos (dev ticket: github:pull/987).

Action items
- @Ethan: run two internal rehearsal demos next week, capture short clip for seller practice.
- @Nina: draft the 10-prompt eval templates for Retail / FinServ.
- @Omar: scope the Console macro PR and add to linked_artifacts.

Notes to self (formatting + copy hooks)
- Keep scripts in the 1–2 sentence per bullet range; sellers memorize rather than read.
- Add short audible cues for SE: "Now I'll trigger fallback" -> helps customer attention.

Relevant refs
- Confluence: GTMP/field-lab-notes-2024 (linked)
- JIRA: GTMP-432 (pilot automation)

End of doc — WIP.

(Quick meta: this is intentionally compact to be usable on calls; expand to slides if the team wants a 5-slide deck forSE training.)
